title: Compressor Discharge Hot
shortDescription: Discharge thermistor exceeded safe operating temperature.
fullDescription: Follett Horizon and Symphony Plus chewblet ice machines monitor compressor discharge temperature. E1 indicates the discharge sensor reached the protective limit. Common causes are restricted airflow, fan failure, or low charge.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Brush and vacuum coil; verify clearances and ambient.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fan rotates freely and runs during operation.

faq.a: At least every 6 months; more often near fryers or grills.

title: Long Freeze Cycle
shortDescription: Freeze cycle did not complete in allotted time.
fullDescription: E2 indicates that the suction line thermistor never reached the freeze setpoint within the cycle timer. Causes include scaling, condenser issues, or refrigeration problems.

fixSteps.title: Inspect condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Clean coil and verify fan operation.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant or auger gearbox work requires service tech.

faq.q: Is descaling safe for the auger?
faq.a: Use only approved nickel-safe cleaners; aggressive acids damage the auger.

title: Auger Motor Overload
shortDescription: Chewblet auger drew excessive current or stalled.
fullDescription: Follett's chewblet ice is formed by a rotating auger inside the evaporator. E3 fires when the auger motor exceeds current limits, often because of ice jam, gearbox wear, or seized bearings.

fixSteps.title: Thaw evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and let evaporator warm up to clear any jam.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gearbox
fixSteps.instruction: Check for oil leaks, abnormal play. Service per Follett bulletin.

whenToCallPro: Auger and gearbox work requires factory-trained service.

faq.a: Often yes, with Follett gearbox kits installed by certified service.

title: Water Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E4 indicates the water level reading is out of range. Without proper water sensing, the unit cannot fill or run safely.

fixSteps.title: Clean probes
fixSteps.instruction: Descale water level probes and reservoir.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Verify harness fully seated and undamaged.

whenToCallPro: Persistent fault after cleaning suggests board issue.

faq.a: No, only Follett-approved cleaners are safe for the system.

title: Bin Full Sensor Failure
fullDescription: Follett uses an infrared eye or thermistor to detect bin level. E5 means the sensor is blocked, dirty, or failed. The machine stops to prevent overflow.

fixSteps.title: Clean lenses
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe IR eye and emitter clean of mineral buildup.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If clean lens still fails, install replacement sensor kit.

whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring are correct, board needs service.

faq.q: How does the IR eye work?
faq.a: Emitter and receiver pair; ice between them blocks beam to indicate full.

title: Compressor Lockout
fullDescription: E6 indicates the compressor has been protected from continuous fault conditions and is locked out. Cycling power without fixing the underlying cause will only repeat the problem.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose root cause
fixSteps.instruction: Refrigeration tech to gauge system, test components.

whenToCallPro: All compressor and refrigerant issues need certified service.

faq.a: Resetting hides the symptom; the cause must be diagnosed first.

title: Communication Loss
shortDescription: Display lost communication with main controller.
fullDescription: E7 indicates broken communication between the user interface and main board. Often a loose harness or moisture intrusion.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and reseat all harnesses on both boards.

faq.a: Yes, surges commonly damage these boards.

title: Cleaning Reminder
fullDescription: Follett units track operating time and prompt cleaning. Performing cleaning on time prevents scale buildup and extends auger and bearing life.

fixSteps.title: Run cleaning cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Use Follett-approved cleaner; follow steps in user manual.

whenToCallPro: Operator-level task; tech only for deep service.

title: Compressor Run Time Exceeded
fullDescription: Follett Horizon E8 indicates the compressor has run beyond its maximum allowable continuous time without satisfying the cycle terminator. Often a sign of low charge, dirty condenser, or a failed thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Note status indicators
fixSteps.instruction: Record what is on the controller display and at what point in the cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect related hardware
fixSteps.instruction: Open service panel and visually inspect the implicated component, cleaning where applicable.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed part
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM Follett replacement, retest cycle.

whenToCallPro: Auger and refrigeration repairs require a trained technician.

faq.q: How serious is E8 on Follett Horizon?
faq.a: Status indicators are informational; faults like E8/E9/E10 must be addressed promptly to avoid damage.
